subject: general
question: In India, who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner?
solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Chief Election Commissioner:**

__
 
• The President appoints Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners.
 
• They have a fixed tenure of six years, or up to the age of 65 years.
 
• The commission consists of one Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners.
 
• Chief Election Commissioner enjoys the same status and receives salary and perks as available to Judges of the Supreme Court of India.​
 
• **Procedure for Removal:**​
 
 
• Chief Election Commissioner may be removed from office through a motion adopted by Parliament on grounds of ‘Proven misbehavior or incapacity.
 
• Removal requires a special majority of 2/3rd members present and voting.
 
• It should be supported by more than 50% of the total strength of the house.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Vice President of India:-**

 
 
• **He is the second-highest constitutional office in the country, after the President. **
 
• The Vice President is elected by an electoral college consisting of the members of both houses of Parliament, the Rajya Sabha (upper house) and the Lok Sabha (lower house).
 
• The Vice President holds office for a term of five years and can be re-elected.
 
 
 
• **Speaker of the Lok Sabha:-**
 
 
• **He is the presiding officer and the highest authority of the Lok Sabha, the lower house of the Parliament of India. **
 
• The Speaker is elected generally in the first meeting of the Lok Sabha following general elections. Serving for a term of five years, the Speaker is chosen from sitting members of the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Prime Minister of India:-**
 
 
• **It is the head of the government of the Republic of India. **
 
• The Prime Minister is appointed by the President of India and must maintain the confidence of the Lok Sabha (lower house of Parliament).
 
• The Prime Minister holds office at the pleasure of the President and can be removed from office if he or she loses the confidence of the Lok Sabha.
